hints: Focus on what warm aqueous silver nitrate is testing for, the release of halide ions to form silver halide precipitates.
Notice compound X has both C-Cl and C-I bonds, but the C-I bond is much weaker and hydrolyses far faster than C-Cl.
Connect the fastest halide released to its precipitate colour, then replace only that one halogen with OH to get the first organic product.
walkthrough:
**Recall the silver nitrate test**

Think of this as a hydrolysis test. Warm aqueous $\text{AgNO}_3$ provides water to replace $\text{C-X}$ with $\text{C-OH}$, and $\text{Ag}^+$ to trap the released $\text{X}^-$.

$$\text{R-X} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{R-OH} + \text{X}^- + \text{H}^+$$
$$\text{Ag}^+ + \text{X}^- \rightarrow \text{AgX(s)}$$

**Decide which halogen leaves first**

Compound X has two $\text{C-Cl}$ bonds and one $\text{C-I}$ bond. Bond strength falls $\text{C-Cl} > \text{C-Br} > \text{C-I}$, so the $\text{C-I}$ bond breaks fastest.

This means $\text{I}^-$ is released immediately, while the $\text{C-Cl}$ bonds stay intact for now.

**Link halide to precipitate colour**

Remember the classic colours: $\text{AgCl}$ is white, $\text{AgBr}$ is cream, $\text{AgI}$ is yellow.

Since $\text{I}^-$ is released first, the immediate precipitate is yellow $\text{AgI}$:
$$\text{Ag}^+ + \text{I}^- \rightarrow \text{AgI(s, yellow)}$$

**Draw the first organic product**

Only the $\text{C-I}$ group is hydrolysed in the first step. It becomes $\text{C-OH}$.

The ring $\text{-Cl}$ and the $\text{-CH}_2\text{Cl}$ group are unchanged, giving a chloro-alcohol product.

options.A: Cream is the colour of AgBr, but there is no bromine in X. The structure also wrongly replaces the secondary C-Cl with OH at the same time as the C-I, but C-Cl hydrolyses much more slowly, so this cannot be the first product.
options.B: Cream again suggests bromide, which is absent. The triol structure shows all three halogens replaced at once, but hydrolysis is stepwise and only the weakest C-I bond reacts immediately.
options.C: White is the colour of AgCl. This would mean a C-Cl bond reacted first, but C-Cl is stronger than C-I. The structure keeps the C-I and replaces a C-Cl, which is the opposite of the correct reactivity order.
options.D: Yellow is correct for AgI formed from the fast release of I-. The organic product correctly shows only the C-I replaced by C-OH, while both the ring Cl and the CH2Cl group remain unchanged. This matches bond strength and stepwise hydrolysis.
